events.title: Alan Turing defines the Turing machine
events.summary: Alan Turing's 1936 paper 'On Computable Numbers' introduced the Turing machine — the theoretical model behind all modern computers.
events.about: Turing formalized what it means to compute, defined decidability limits, and influenced von Neumann architecture. Every programming language and CPU is an approximation of his abstract machine.

narrative.whyChosen: The Turing machine is the conceptual root of computer science.
narrative.whyImportant: It linked logic, mathematics, and mechanical computation.
narrative.problemSolved: Mathematicians needed a precise definition of effective calculability.
